clue.text: Hard work is what might get you a job

definitions.text: what might get you a job
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a formal request submitted to an employer

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as advice that effort lands jobs; in fact the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sustained diligence and the form a candidate submits when seeking employment.

clue.text: Scotsman caught breaking tech company's gizmo

indicators.note: the Scotsman and the catch break into the company name, splitting it apart

parts.note: Apple is the American technology company
Ian is a typically Scottish first name
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Scot is caught hacking a tech firm's gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a household device or machine, the same idea as a gadget.

clue.text: Don't fail to include game in meat-filled snacks?

indicators.note: the word for passing takes the game inside itself

parts.note: to pass a test is not to fail it
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: An instruction to make sure a game features among your pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasties are pastry parcels, typically filled with meat and vegetables, eaten as a snack or light meal.

clue.text: Cunning crossword compiler, one using anagrams

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: the compiler uses anagrams, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for a clever setter who relies on anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious and cunning both describe something cleverly devised and inventive.

clue.text: Endless regret after a love affair

indicators.note: the shortened regret follows the letter A
without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to mourn is to regret a loss

explanation.surface: Remorse that follows a romantic fling.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a borrowed French word for a romance, often a secret or illicit one.

clue.text: Regularly find kid on Twitch silly

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: Seeking out a youngster on the streaming site Twitch looks foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic and silly both mean stupid or foolish.

clue.text: The Darkness or Sir Elton John, say, on the radio

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard, not read, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: Elton John is a knight, holding the title Sir

explanation.surface: Two rock acts, the band The Darkness and Elton John, being played on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Darkness is also a British rock band, which makes the surface read as music radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark period between sunset and dawn.

clue.text: Shows amazement, back inside Japanese pagoda

indicators.note: the concealed letters are read from right to left
the letters sit within the words Japanese pagoda

explanation.surface: A tourist marvels within a pagoda in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed in wonder or astonishment.

clue.text: Inexperienced goalie is tender of course

parts.note: green means new and untrained
the goalkeeper is the keeper

explanation.surface: A novice goalkeeper is, naturally, gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally', but the course is a golf course and the tender is one who tends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenkeeper looks after the turf of a golf course or bowling green.

clue.text: Ageing doctor keeps arguing, you heard

indicators.note: the doctor holds the other parts inside

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner
rowing (rhyming with cowing) means quarrelling

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word sounds like a single letter

parts.note: said aloud, you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: An elderly doctor keeps on bickering, as you have heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing up is maturing, getting older as a child becomes an adult.

clue.text: Portray pope, possibly, as a killjoy

indicators.note: these letters could possibly be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An artist might paint the pontiff as a spoilsport.
explanation.definitionFit: A party-pooper is someone who spoils others' fun, exactly what a killjoy does.

clue.text: Leader deserts mutiny, creating issue

indicators.note: the first letter leaves the word

parts.note: sedition is incitement to rebellion

explanation.surface: The ringleader abandons a revolt, causing a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one issue of a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Spinning object unchanged when spun around?

definitions.text: Spinning object unchanged when spun around?

parts.words: Spinning object unchanged when spun around?
parts.note: the clue describes a thing that turns and whose name reads identically backwards, a palindrome

explanation.surface: A riddle about a turning thing that looks the same after a rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is anything that rotates, a thing that spins on an axis.

clue.text: Things you can't do with child, running around

indicators.note: the combined letters are turned around, read backwards

parts.note: a son is a male child
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Activities forbidden when a toddler is dashing about.
explanation.definitionFit: No-nos are forbidden actions, things which are not allowed.

clue.text: Concerned with smell round large manufacturing plant

parts.note: O is round in shape
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a factory is a manufacturing plant

explanation.surface: A smelly big factory nearby causes concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Olfactory is the adjective relating to the sense of smell.

clue.text: Warning corrupt state, giving hint of what's to come

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning

indicators.note: corrupted letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a corrupt regime signals worse ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample or glimpse of something yet to happen.

clue.text: Hope very crooked Democrat is promoted, inappropriately

indicators.note: bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: A wish that a dishonest Democrat gets advanced unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhyped means publicised or praised far more than is warranted, an excessive kind of promotion.

clue.text: Person working out tax without hesitation, right?

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the tax goes around the hesitation

parts.note: excise is a duty on goods
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone calculating a tax promptly, a quick query for confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' looks like doing sums, but means exercising.
explanation.definitionFit: An exerciser is someone doing physical training, who works out.

clue.text: Warm drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: friendly and genial, as an adjective
second meaning: a fruit-flavoured beverage, diluted to drink

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a hot drink, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a friendly manner and also names a sweet concentrated beverage.

clue.text: Look after bishop's territory as well, we hear

indicators.note: said aloud, the words sound like the answer

parts.note: a see is the diocese a bishop governs; too means also, as well

explanation.surface: Caring for a diocese as an extra duty, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to something is to attend to it or take care of it.

clue.text: Cleaner of Barnet Post Office wearing fake ring

indicators.note: the fake ring is worn around the post office abbreviation

parts.note: a sham is a fake
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A post office cleaner in Barnet, a London district, sporting a fake ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the north London district, but in Cockney rhyming slang Barnet (from Barnet Fair) means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is the liquid used to wash hair, so it cleans one's barnet.

clue.text: Flipping cheek, forbidding traveller to Mecca?

indicators.note: flipped over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lip is insolence or cheek
grim means stern and forbidding

explanation.surface: A cross complaint about rudeness that bars someone from travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim makes a religious journey, as Muslims do on the hajj to Mecca; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Heads for loss, if doubling one's stake in the pools

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Doubling one's bet on the football pools invites a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The pools here are the football pools betting game in the surface, but swimming pools in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: French artist working in New York gallery

indicators.note: the working word sits inside the gallery name

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A French painter exhibiting at a New York gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of the Water Lilies series.

clue.text: Rogue hates work in cafe

indicators.note: rogue letters go astray, so these are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A villain hates having a job at a cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea shop is a small restaurant serving tea and light refreshments.

clue.text: Big stars dare Sting to get a makeover

indicators.note: a makeover changes the look, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Celebrities challenge the singer Sting to be restyled.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars suggests celebrities like Sting, but they are astronomical.
explanation.definitionFit: Red giants are large luminous stars late in their lives, swollen and cool.

clue.text: Telegraph, say, or what spin doctors do receiving copy

indicators.note: the public relations letters take the copy inside

parts.note: spin doctors do PR, public relations
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: This newspaper, or the press office, getting a story to print.
explanation.definitionFit: The Telegraph is a British daily newspaper, an example of a paper.

clue.text: Croatian port getting support in a jiffy

parts.note: Split is a port city on Croatia's Dalmatian coast
to second a motion is to support it

explanation.surface: A Croatian harbour wins backing very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is a tiny instant, as brief a moment as a jiffy.
